diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, as a special case of Theorem 2 in {\rm \cite{griebel2023analysis}}, for a given function $f(x_1,x_2)\in L^2([a,b]^2)$
where for each $n$, the left eigenfunctions $\{\phi_{i_n}^{(n)}\}_{i_n=1}^{+\infty}$ form a orthonormal basis in $L^2([a,b])$

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in L^2 only forces the coefficients in any orthonormal basis to be square-summable; no algebraic decay is implied. The rate I_n >= (1/epsilon)^{1/alpha} yields error <= sqrt(2) epsilon only under an alpha-Sobolev-type hypothesis (coefficient decay |c_i| = O(i^{-alpha-1/2})). For a general L^2 function (e.g., coefficients decaying like i^{-1}(log i)^{-1}, which are square-summable) the Fourier tail has no power rate, so the stated implication is false as written.

failure_location.quote: for a given function $f(x_1,x_2)\in L^2([a,b]^2)$, when for each $n$, $I_n\geq (1/\epsilon)^{1/\alpha}$, one has $\|Ff(x_1,x_2)-f(x_1,x_2)\|_{L^2}\leq \sqrt{2}\epsilon$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing smoothness hypothesis on f (e.g., f in the alpha-Sobolev space associated with the eigenbasis, as in the cited Theorem 2 of griebel2023analysis), or delete the quantitative implication.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative guarantee in this unlabelled remark is false for general L^2 functions; no labelled result depends on it, but the remark misstates the hypotheses under which the sqrt(2) epsilon bound holds.
issues.title: False sqrt(2)epsilon rate for general L^2 functions in the remark after Theorem t-lasso:general-theorem-main
issues.why_classification: Contained to an illustrative remark with no dependents; the repair is the addition of the standard smoothness hypothesis, and no theorem or algorithm relies on the claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the proof is complete by combining Theorems \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} and \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-main}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only invokes Theorem t-lasso:general-theorem-main, whose bound is C min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha; the stated max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha} is stronger and false. Counterexample: take f independent of x_1 with coefficients supported on |k_2|>I_2 decaying like |k_2|^{-alpha-1}; then f is in H^alpha and its coefficient matrix A is zero (all modes lie outside the truncation box), so Ff=0 and ||Ff-f|| ~ I_2^{-alpha-1/2}, while C max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha = C I_1^{-alpha} -> 0 as I_1 grows with I_2 fixed. The truncation error is governed by the coarser (smaller) truncation parameter.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace max{I_1,I_2} by min{I_1,I_2} in the theorem statement and in Corollary cor:added-1; the existing proof via Theorem t-lasso:general-theorem-main then yields exactly the stated bound.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Fourier-tail rate in Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main and in Corollary cor:added-1 is false; the correct rate is governed by min{I_1,I_2}.
issues.title: Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main states the Fourier-tail rate with max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}; the correct rate is min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha} and the max version is false
issues.why_classification: A one-word correction to the true rate; the comparable min-rate result survives and no valid content is lost, since the max-rate claim was simply false.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own Parseval identity, ||F~f-Ff||_{L^2} = ||A-EF*||_F exactly, and the Frobenius norm is always at least the max norm, so the claimed inequality is backwards. Concrete counterexample: A-EF* equal to delta times the all-ones matrix of size (2I_1+1)x(2I_2+1) has max norm delta but Frobenius norm delta*sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)). Hence the term epsilon||A||_2 in the theorem (and the sigma_{S_2+1}(A) term in Corollary cor:added-1) is not established; the proof only supports an additional factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invoked max-norm epsilon-rank result (Theorem t-lasso:epsilonrank-main) by a Frobenius-norm low-rank guarantee (e.g., the randomized SVD already surveyed in the paper) giving ||A-EF*||_F <= epsilon||A||_F, so Parseval yields the comparable bound epsilon||A||_F; alternatively weaken the second term by the factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)).
issues.overall_effect: The headline error bound of Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main and the second term of Corollary cor:added-1 are unproven as stated; the proofs yield a bound worse by the factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)).
issues.title: Proof of Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main uses the backwards inequality ||F~f-Ff||_{L^2} <= ||A-EF*||_max; Parseval gives equality with the Frobenius norm
issues.why_classification: No one-line fix exists: restoring the advertised guarantee requires substituting a different invoked result (randomized SVD-type Frobenius bound) or accepting a dimension-factor weakening; a recognizably comparable bound survives, so it is not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the rank of $\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{C}^{S_2\times S_1}$ is less than or equal to $R$ with $\min\{S_1,S_2\}> R$

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (t-lasso:method-one:sub3-main) defines G as an S_1 x S_2 matrix (rows indexed by s_1 in T_1, columns by s_2 in T_2), so G^\dag is S_2 x S_1 and (G^\dag)(j_1,j_2) requires j_1 <= S_2; likewise C has S_2 columns and R has S_1 rows, so phi_{j_1}^{(1)} needs j_1 <= S_2 and phi_{j_2}^{(2)} needs j_2 <= S_1. The displayed sum ranges j_1 to S_1 and j_2 to S_2, making the formula ill-defined, and the product C·G^\dag·R in the same paragraph is also dimensionally inconsistent with the stated G in C^{S_2 x S_1}. The forced correction is G in C^{S_1 x S_2} and summation ranges j_1=1..S_2, j_2=1..S_1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the size of G to S_1 x S_2 and swap the summation limits to j_1=1..S_2, j_2=1..S_1.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed formula defining the CUR-based approximation F~f is ill-defined as written; the algorithms' output contract (forming F~f from {C,U,R}) relies on the corrected reading.
issues.title: Equation (t-lasso:approximation-expression-general-v2-main) and the Section 4 introduction state inconsistent dimensions for G and for the index ranges of the double sum
issues.why_classification: The single forced correction is determined by dimensional consistency with the definitions of C, G, R; no inference or construction needs further repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d), where $0<\tau<1$ is a given parameter.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop continues while tol > tau OR k <= K, i.e., it exits only when tol <= tau AND k > K. Consequently (i) the tolerance can never trigger early stopping: the loop always executes at least K+1 iterations, so the quoted counts with S_n = 2Kb_n+1 are not guaranteed; and (ii) once k > K the only active condition is tol > tau, so the 'maximum number of iterations K' is not a cap and the loop never terminates if the tolerance is never met. The intended condition is 'tol > tau AND k <= K' (stop when tol <= tau or k > K).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change 'or' to 'and' in the WHILE condition of all three algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithms t-lasso:alg1-main, t-lasso:alg2-main and t-lasso:alg1:app-main lose their adaptive termination guarantee and their advertised integral counts; non-termination is possible for the latter two when the tolerance is never satisfied.
issues.title: All three algorithms use WHILE 'tol > tau or k <= K', so the maximum iteration count K is ineffective, early stopping on the tolerance never occurs, and non-termination is possible
issues.why_classification: A one-word correction restores the intended adaptive behavior and all advertised counts; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\|< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d)

issues.failure_explanation: The specification continues while max{sigma_min(C)^2/nF_C, sigma_min(R)^2/nF_R} >= tau^2, i.e., stops only when both ratios are below tau^2; the code stops as soon as min{sigma_min(C)/sqrt(nF_C), sigma_min(R)/sqrt(nF_R)} < tau, i.e., when only one ratio is below tau^2. Since min <= max, the implemented rule terminates strictly earlier than specified and can stop while the other ratio is still >= tau^2. (In practice this is currently masked by the WHILE 'or' defect, which prevents any early stopping.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace min by max in the computation of tol (equivalently, restate the prose criterion with min).
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm as written does not implement its own termination criterion, so the adaptive rank decision differs from the stated one.
issues.title: Algorithm t-lasso:alg1-main implements the stopping rule with min{·} although its specification requires max{·}
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix reconciles the code with its specification; the stopping rule is a heuristic with no formal guarantee attached, so nothing further is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \STATE Compute $\mathbf{G}_{1k}$, $\mathbf{G}_{2k}$, and $\mathbf{G}_{3k}$ according to (\ref{t-lasso:method-one:sub3-main}) with $\{\mathbb{T}_1,\mathbb{T}_2'\}$, $\{\mathbb{T}_1',\mathbb{T}_2\}$, and $\{\mathbb{T}_1',\mathbb{T}_2'\}$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Because T_n is never updated from {0}, every block G_{1k}, G_{2k} is computed against the singleton sets (so the assembled G is not the coefficient submatrix A(T_1,T_2)), and at the end C is computed with T_2 = {0} (a single column) and R with T_1 = {0} (a single row), while U = G^\dag has size S_2 x S_1; hence C·U·R and the function F~f in (t-lasso:approximation-expression-general-v2-main) cannot be formed from the output. The prose description and Algorithm t-lasso:alg1-main both contain the update T_n = T_n ∪ T_n'; the pseudocode of Algorithm t-lasso:alg2-main and of t-lasso:alg1:app-main drops it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we need to obtain three matrices $\mathbf{G}_{1k}\in\mathbb{C}^{(2(k-1)b_1+1)\times 2b_2}$, $\mathbf{G}_{2k}\in\mathbb{C}^{2b_1\times (2(k-1)b_2+1)}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{3k}\in\mathbb{C}^{2b_1\times 2b_2}$
b) for each $k\geq 1$, to update ${\rm nF}_{\mathbf{G}}$ requires $8b_1b_2(2k-1)+4(b_1+b_2)$ operations

issues.failure_explanation: The block sizes give (2(k-1)b_1+1)(2b_2) + (2b_1)(2(k-1)b_2+1) + (2b_1)(2b_2) = 4(2k-1)b_1b_2 + 2(b_1+b_2) integrals per iteration (for k=1 this is 4b_1b_2 + 2(b_1+b_2), not 2(b_1+b_2)). The paper's own complexity line 8b_1b_2(2k-1)+4(b_1+b_2), twice the entry count, confirms the correct figure. The final total (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2 is nonetheless correct, because sum_{k=1}^K 4(2k-1)b_1b_2 = 4K^2 b_1b_2.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: that is, the number of double integrals in Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg1:app-main} is less than Algorithms \ref{t-lasso:alg1-main} and \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main}.

issues.failure_explanation: Building G costs 1+4Kb_1b_2 integrals (the off-diagonal blocks are fabricated zeros). If C and R are computed as true coefficient matrices (the only reading under which the CUR product C·G^\dag·R keeps its meaning), the 1+4Kb_1b_2 genuinely computed diagonal-block entries can be reused, giving the total (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-1-4Kb_1b_2, which exceeds the (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2 integrals of Algorithms t-lasso:alg1-main/t-lasso:alg2-main by S_1S_2-1-4Kb_1b_2 = 4K(K-1)b_1b_2+2K(b_1+b_2) > 0. If instead the fabricated zero blocks are reused for C and R, the total is (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-2S_1S_2+1+4Kb_1b_2, still not the stated formula (which carries +Kb_1b_2), and C, R cease to be true submatrices of A. Either way the stated count and the advertised reduction are incorrect.
